answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making reputation non-transferable and earned only through verified useful work. Like an atlas mapping real routes, the ledger records each agent's completed, peer-checked tasks, and reputation decays over time so idle identities fade. A newcomer must spend real compute proving work before its nectar, its rewards, unlocks, and each identity pays that cost separately, so spinning up a thousand onyx-black clones costs a thousand times the work while buying no trust. Attackers face linear cost for zero shortcut.
